Laura —

I reviewed telemetry and the serving traces. There was a KV cache thrash combined with a higher-than-expected concurrent prefix expansion from FastRetail's batch operation. Net result: we saw the 99.9th percentile latency exceed the contracted threshold for 32 minutes. This does meet the SLA breach definition.

Suggested remediation steps already taken:
- Applied an emergency routing rule to avoid the affected host pool (completed 11/27 02:10 PST)
- Rebalanced KV allocations and increased shard headroom (completed 11/28)
- Added a temporary request-level retry for non-idempotent checkout flows (rolled back after validation)

Implications for concession: engineering impact is limited to that short window — but I recommend a concession that acknowledges the business impact without setting a broad precedent. My recommended package (technical + commercial):
1) One-time invoice credit equivalent to 25% of the monthly bill for the impacted month (calculated pro-rata to the 32-minute window), capped at $40,000.
2) One month of free premium support (no charge) to cover the validation window.
3) A joint postmortem and a “safety plan” delivered within 10 business days.

If sales wants to be more generous for relationship reasons, we can escalate for an exception to increase the cap.

Rishi
Director, Applied ML & Reliability
